title: Canons of interpreting the Decalogue; Cap.8 next on ceremonial law
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): If it happens that two precepts cannot be observed at once, regard stands as had toward that which stands as belonging toward greater moment. — When one relative stands as commanded or forbidden by a precept, ye other also stands as commanded or forbidden. — An effect stands as commanded and forbidden in its cause, and a cause in its effect. — Homogeneous and related actions stand as commanded or forbidden by ye same precept. — In an affirmation ye opposite negation stands as comprehended, and in a negation ye opposite affirmation, because God demands not only abstinence from evil but also ye doing belonging toward good. — CHAPTER EIGHT follows, On ye ceremonial law.
pass_b_english: In an affirmation the opposite negation is comprehended, and in a negation the opposite affirmation, because God demands not only abstinence from evil but also the doing of good. Homogeneous and related actions are commanded or forbidden by the same precept. An effect is commanded and forbidden in its cause, and a cause in its effect. When one relative is commanded or forbidden by a precept, the other also is commanded or forbidden. If it happens that two precepts cannot be observed at once, regard is had to that which is of greater moment.
CHAPTER EIGHT follows, On the ceremonial law.
source_text: In affirmatione negatio, & in negatione affirmatio opposita comprehenditur, quia Deus non solum abstinentiam a malo verum etiam efficientiam boni postulat. Actiones homogeneae & cognatae eodem praecepto iubentur aut vetantur. Effectus in sua causa, & causa in suo effectu iubetur & prohibetur. Relativo uno praecepto vel prohibito, etiam alterum praecipitur vel prohibetur. Si contingat duorum praeceptorum observationem simul praestari non posse, eius habetur ratio quod momenti maioris est. CAPUT OCTAVUM sequitur, De lege cerimoniali.
